Energy Consumption & Grid Load Patterns

Session energy is stable across location and time segments, so grid stress is mainly a function of simultaneous demand/load timing rather than larger per-session charging volumes. Peak periods have the clearest grid load exposure.

Peak load step-change. Peak mean load is 84.1 kW, compared with 34.7 kW off-peak.
Daily variation is secondary. The day/time matrix shows the same broad load pattern across all weekdays present in the data.
Energy per session is consistent. Average energy stays near 39.1 kWh, making scheduling and load balancing more important than vehicle mix alone.

Renewable Energy Integration & Dynamic Pricing

Renewable energy ratio deserves prominent operating attention: it is higher in off-peak periods and is strongly positively associated with optimization reward (correlation 0.590). Electricity price, however, is effectively flat across demand conditions in this dataset.

Optimization Insights & Recommendations

The optimization strategy should combine peak load reduction, local queue hotspot relief, and green-time incentives. These recommendations are grounded in observed data patterns and avoid extrapolating beyond the CSV.

Queue Add targeted bottleneck controls

  • Prioritize operational review at ST004 / Highway, ST009 / Urban, and ST017 / Highway, the highest average-wait station/location segments.
  • Use reservation pacing or dispatch guidance when queue length reaches local thresholds, because aggregate queue length is flat but station-level wait hotspots persist.
  • Monitor P90 wait, not only mean wait, because customer pain emerges at tail wait times.

Load Shift flexible sessions out of peak

  • Peak mean load exceeds off-peak by 49.4 kW; use app prompts, managed charging, and fleet scheduling to move flexible sessions to off-peak windows.
  • Focus load balancing on time slot first, then station segment, because location-type differences are small compared with the peak/off-peak load gap.
  • Use station demand ranking to sequence capacity expansion at high-demand segments such as ST012 / Highway.

Renewables Incentivize green charging windows

  • Promote off-peak charging as the default green option: off-peak renewable ratio is 39.3%, versus 29.0% in peak periods.
  • Use weather/time renewable ratio monitoring to publish “green charging” prompts when renewable availability is strongest.
  • Pair renewable-heavy windows with queue-aware scheduling so sustainability gains do not create new local waiting bottlenecks.

Pricing Make dynamic pricing operational

  • The observed peak/off-peak price difference is only -0.03, while peak reward is -12.75 lower than off-peak; revise tariffs to reflect grid stress.
  • Offer off-peak or high-renewable discounts and peak surcharges for non-urgent charging, while protecting high-priority sessions.
  • Track conversion: measure whether price changes reduce peak demand and improve optimization reward without increasing average wait.

Methodology & Data Integrity Notes

  • Primary source: /app/benchmark/data.csv; dataset contains 8,354 rows and 27 columns with no missing values detected.
  • Temporal columns were parsed from source strings, and all KPIs were computed directly from row-level records.
  • Required segmentation dimensions were applied where present: location type, vehicle type, time slot, day of week, and weather condition.
  • Expected categories absent from the data are explicitly noted: location type Suburban; time slot Mid-Peak.
  • The dataset is documented as synthetic/simulated; recommendations should be validated with live operational telemetry before capital deployment.
